name: Routes & Networks
lesson: A network has vertices (dots) joined by edges (lines). The degree of a vertex is the number of edges meeting it. Crossings without dots are not extra vertices.
Every edge contributes 2 to the total of all degrees, one at each end. A connected network with no cycles is called a tree. A tree on $n$ vertices has $n-1$ edges.

A one-stroke walk uses every edge exactly once. In a connected network it is possible when there are exactly 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree. With 2 odd vertices, the walk starts at one and ends at the other.

problems.q: In the network, how many edges meet vertex A?
problems.hint: Count only the lines ending at A.
problems.solution: The edges AB, AD and AC meet A, so A has degree 3.
problems.imageAlt: Four vertices A, B, C, D form a square with edges AB, BC, CD, DA and diagonal AC.

problems.q: What is the sum of the degrees of all four vertices in the network?
problems.hint: Count each edge at both of its ends.
problems.solution: There are 5 edges. Each contributes 2 to the degree total, so the sum is 10.
problems.imageAlt: Four vertices A, B, C, D form a square with edges AB, BC, CD, DA and diagonal AC.

problems.q: Four towns each have a direct road to every other town. There is one road for each pair of towns. How many roads are there?
problems.hint: Count pairs of towns rather than directions of travel.
problems.solution: Each of 4 towns meets 3 roads, counting each road twice. There are $4\times3\div2=6$ roads.

problems.q: What is the fewest roads needed to connect five towns so that every town can be reached from every other?
problems.hint: A chain of towns gives one possible construction.
problems.solution: Starting with one town, each of the other four needs a connection. Four roads suffice, for example in a chain, and fewer cannot connect all five towns.

problems.q: A network has a total vertex degree of 18. How many edges does it have?
problems.solution: Each edge contributes 2 to the degree total, so there are $18\div2=9$ edges.

problems.q: A one-stroke walk must use each edge exactly once. In this network, which vertices can be the starting point?
problems.hint: Find the vertices of odd degree.
problems.solution: A and C each have degree 3; B and D each have degree 2. A one-stroke walk must start at A or C and finish at the other. For example, A-B-C-D-A-C works.
problems.imageAlt: Square network with one diagonal AC; degrees of A and C are odd.

problems.q: Can this network be drawn in one stroke, using each edge exactly once? The crossing of the diagonals is not a vertex.
problems.solution: Each of the four vertices has degree 3. A one-stroke walk can have only 0 or 2 odd-degree vertices, so this network is impossible.
problems.imageAlt: Four corner vertices of a square joined by all six edges; the diagonal crossing has no dot.

problems.q: The numbers on the roads are their lengths. What is the length of the shortest route from A to D?
problems.hint: Compare routes through B and C.
problems.solution: Route A-B-C-D has length $2+1+2=5$. A-C-D has length 7 and A-B-D has length 8, so 5 is shortest.
problems.imageAlt: Network with road lengths AB=2, AC=5, BC=1, BD=6 and CD=2.

problems.q: Five towns each have a direct road to every other town, one road per pair. How many roads are there?
problems.hint: Count four connections per town, then remove double-counting.

problems.q: A network's four vertex degrees are 1, 2, 2 and 3. How many edges does it have?
problems.hint: Add all the degrees and divide by 2.

problems.q: Nine towns are connected by a tree: a connected road network containing no cycle. One road is removed. How many connected groups of towns remain?
problems.hint: In a tree there is exactly one route between any pair of towns.
problems.solution: Removing one road breaks the only route between its two sides. Each side remains connected, producing exactly two groups.

problems.q: Can a network have exactly three vertices of odd degree? Explain.
problems.hint: Consider whether the total of all degrees would be even or odd.
problems.solution: Three odd degrees add to an odd number. Adding any even degrees keeps it odd. But every edge contributes 2 to the total, which must therefore be even. This is impossible.
